frostwater_shelf.why: 'kelp forests on cold_ocean shelf and slope (y28-58)', 'seagrass on cold_ocean shelf; none under frozen_ocean'; frozen_ocean is 'north of z1300, 120 or more blocks from land' and deep_frozen_ocean 'north of z1300 where the planned seabed is at or below y36' (data/regions.json biomes.rules), and nothing grows under either (OCEAN.md: kelp 'not warm or frozen', seagrass 'every ocean except frozen')

windward_deep.why: 'kelp on the shelf and upper slope', 'seagrass on the shelf', 'no coral'

eastern_reach.why: 'kelp and seagrass on the shelf', 'no coral (lukewarm_ocean does not grow it in vanilla)'

southern_shallows.why: 'seagrass across the shelf; no kelp in warm_ocean', and warm_ocean is 'shelf within 220 blocks of land', so kelp only on the lukewarm outer shelf beyond it (OCEAN.md: kelp grows in lukewarm). The coral reefs this region's flora names are NOT built: data/spawn_block_policy.json whitelists live coral for cobblers_sea_life's Relic reef only, and widening that is the owner's decision (WATER_LIFE_GAP.md)

land_distance.why: every distance rule (shelf width, the frozen line, the warm line, a shaped coast's reach) is decided on the EXACT Euclidean distance to the nearest land column wherever a cheap first guess cannot settle it. The guess: distance on a 4-block grid (a coarse cell is land if any column in it is), chamfer, converged out to max_blocks; the truth lies in [guess / chamfer_ratio - 3*sqrt2, guess + 3*sqrt2] (beyond max_blocks: at least max_blocks / chamfer_ratio - 3*sqrt2, past every rule). Where a rule's threshold falls inside that interval the column's exact distance is computed: a per-x pass (distance along z to land, capped at column_cap_blocks), then the minimum over dx of dx^2 + that^2. On 2026-10-04 the guess alone overshot (tools/sea_floor_audit.py): 1,149 columns in frozen water (to 123.2 against 120), 460 kelp columns inside the warm line (to 214.2 against 220), 811 beyond a shelf width by up to 3

ownership.sea_life_coast_boxes_from: data/water_shape.json coasts.flats and coasts.skerries, the coasts data/sea_life.json shore.coasts names
ownership.sea_life_coast_boxes_edges: inclusive, x0 <= x <= x1 and z0 <= z <= z1, as tools/water_shape.py reads a box
ownership.pacifidlog_from: every `rect` in data/sea_town.json (districts, rafts, bridges, walks, jetties), grown by data/sea_life.json exclusions.pacifidlog_margin_blocks, edges inclusive: sea_life's exclusion boxes only the deck, and the walks and jetties reach past it
ownership.why: cobblers_sea_life owns the five shaped coasts out to its kelp reach and the Relic reef; this pack writes nowhere in a coast box (edges inclusive) within that reach plus coast_margin_blocks of land (exact distance), nowhere within the reef's outer radius plus the drop plus this margin, and in no column within sea_life_margin_blocks of any cell that pack writes. So the two packs share no column. Pacifidlog's every rect and its margin are kept clear too

kelp.why: kelp forests on the seabed from y28 to y58 (OCEAN.md section 4's kelp row) in patches seen from a boat. A top never within 2 of the surface (at most sea - 3, the threshold both water-life audits hold), so kelp is never a rest point on any crossing; age 25 so it never grows past that. Height is a share of the room between the seabed and that top

seagrass.why: seagrass meadows on the seabed from y40 to y60 (OCEAN.md's seagrass row), dense inside a meadow with a few holes; some tall where there are at least two blocks of water. Never inside a gate line's clearance (tools/sea_life.py's rule for its own seagrass)

writes.why: every write is a `fill ... replace minecraft:water`: it can only turn sea water into a plant, never overwrite a block another pack or an earlier pass put there that no data file lists (CLAUDE.md 'Our list is not the world')

budget.why: a ceiling the build fails closed on: about two and a half times the lake skin's 337,275 commands, because every dressed chunk is loaded once by the step that runs it
